```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(scales)

msrp_df <- read_csv("data/processed/msrp_merged.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
trends_df <- read_csv("data/processed/epa_trends_clean.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

n_msrp <- nrow(msrp_df)
n_years_epa <- n_distinct(trends_df$year)
```

## Horsepower vs. MSRP by Vehicle Body Style

::: {.plot-container}
```{r}
#| label: fig-hp-msrp

# Prepare hover text for interactive exploration
plot_df <- msrp_df |>
  mutate(
    hover_label = paste0(
      "<b>", year, " ", make, " ", model, "</b><br>",
      "Body Style: ", body_style, " (", body_group, ")<br>",
      "Horsepower: ", comma(horsepower), " hp<br>",
      "MSRP: ", dollar(msrp), "<br>",
      "Fuel Economy: ", mpg_city, " city / ", mpg_highway, " hwy MPG"
    )
  )

p_home <- ggplot(
  plot_df,
  aes(
    x = horsepower,
    y = msrp,
    color = body_group,
    text = hover_label
  )
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.55, size = 1.7) +
  scale_y_log10(
    labels = label_dollar(),
    breaks = c(10000, 25000, 50000, 100000, 250000, 500000, 1500000)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Coupe" = "#d90429",
    "Convertible" = "#ef233c",
    "Sedan" = "#9e1b32",
    "Hatchback" = "#ff5964",
    "Wagon" = "#6d6d6d",
    "SUV" = "#111111",
    "Van / Minivan" = "#4a4a4a",
    "Pickup" = "#262626"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Vehicle Sticker Price Rises Steeply With Horsepower (N = ", comma(n_msrp), " Vehicles)"),
    x = "Engine Horsepower (HP)",
    y = "Manufacturer Suggested Retail Price (MSRP, log scale)",
    color = "Body Style"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

ggplotly(p_home, tooltip = "text", height = 460) |>
  layout(
    autosize = TRUE,
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = -0.18),
    margin = list(t = 45, r = 20, b = 75, l = 70)
  ) |>
  config(responsive = TRUE)
```
:::

This chart compares engine horsepower with vehicle MSRP across body styles. Higher-horsepower vehicles generally cost more, while the log scale makes everyday cars easier to compare with high-performance vehicles.
